comparable_cases.case_name: O (a minor) v Great Ormond Street Hospital for Children NHS Trust
comparable_cases.injury_description: a boy of 10 years old at the time of accident, who suffered a 2-degree burn or 2 per cent burn to his back during a 41/2 hour neurosurgical operation. Later on he had to undergo skin grafting operation for the wound to his back from skin grafted from skin on his thigh. The result of the injuries restricted his ability to run and play football, his back was tight and pulled, causing pain when he bent down or stretched his arms.

burn injuries to the dorsum of both hands, face and right side of his back and right elbow in an explosion at work. The burns were over 8 or 9 per cent of his skin. He returned to work after 16 weeks. He also suffered from depression.

a four-year-old girl's injuries included three laceration wounds over both thighs and multiple minor bites and scratch marks over her thighs and left arm. One year after the accident she was found to have various faint scars and two noticeable pairs of stitch marks on the back of her upper thigh. The scars were said would become less noticeable in time. Permanent cosmetic disability was assessed at a quarter per cent. She also suffered from phobia towards dogs, had nightmares. Her psychiatric disability was assessed at 2 per cent of the whole person.
